title: Precision geometry
intro: Dimensional measurements describe both a value and the conditions under which it was obtained.
facts: A measurement needs a unit.
Resolution and accuracy are different properties.

A coating and its substrate behave as a system.
A finish should be described with a measurement method.

intro: An optical assembly combines geometry, alignment and the properties of its materials.
facts: Focal length describes the optical power of a lens.

Reflections depend on angle and surface treatment.

Filtering changes the frequency content of a signal.

intro: Thermal behaviour depends on energy transfer, boundary conditions and the materials involved.
facts: Heat transfer can occur through conduction, convection and radiation.

Transient measurements require a time reference.

title: Circuit fundamentals
intro: A circuit description connects component behaviour with the relationships between voltage and current.
facts: Resistance is measured in ohms.

A schematic describes connections rather than physical placement.
Component tolerances affect the behaviour of an assembly.

title: Robotic mechanisms
intro: A robotic mechanism combines mechanical structure, actuation, sensing and control.
facts: A joint constrains the relative motion of connected parts.

Coordinate frames describe the position of components.

title: Acoustic spaces

title: Energy systems
intro: Energy-system studies compare storage, conversion and losses within a clearly defined boundary.

A comparison needs consistent operating conditions.

title: Imaging methods

facts: Exposure time affects motion blur.

A calibration target provides a repeatable reference.
Contrast depends on both the scene and the imaging system.

title: Astronomical observations
intro: An observing record relates an instrument setup to a position, a time and the conditions of observation.
facts: An angular field of view describes an area of sky.
Long exposures can reveal motion or tracking differences.
Instrument settings should accompany an observing record.
A chart and a photograph represent observations differently.

title: Manufacturing notes
intro: A manufacturing record connects design intent with process settings and observations.
facts: A tolerance defines an allowed dimensional interval.
A fixture constrains a workpiece during an operation.

Inspection criteria should be established before comparison.

title: Structural forms
intro: Structural studies consider geometry, material properties and the conditions of loading.
facts: A load path describes how forces pass through a structure.

title: Computational models
intro: A computational model makes assumptions explicit and represents relationships in a form that can be evaluated.

A numerical approximation introduces discretisation choices.
A result should be interpreted alongside its assumptions.
A repeatable calculation records its parameters.

title: Laboratory practice
intro: A useful laboratory record captures the setup, procedure, observations and limits of an investigation.
facts: A reference sample supports comparison.
A procedure should identify the variables it changes.
An observation is distinct from an interpretation.
A record is more useful when its conditions are explicit.

title: Landscape photography
intro: A landscape photograph brings together light, viewpoint and the time spent observing a place.
facts: The direction of light changes the appearance of a landscape.

A foreground can give a photograph a sense of scale.
Weather and season influence both colour and contrast.

title: Typography studies
intro: Typography gives written language a visual rhythm through letterforms, spacing and arrangement.

Spacing helps separate groups of information.

title: Ceramic forms
intro: Ceramic objects bring together the character of a material and the choices made while shaping it.

A sketch can help compare the proportions of a form.

title: Coffee notebooks
intro: A coffee notebook is a place to record a brewing method, its conditions and the impressions it produces.
facts: Grind size influences the way water passes through coffee.

A tasting note describes an impression rather than a universal judgement.

title: Seasonal kitchen
intro: A seasonal kitchen starts with ingredients, simple preparations and attention to texture and flavour.
facts: A recipe is easier to repeat when quantities and timing are recorded.

Texture and temperature shape the experience of a dish.
Preparing ingredients before cooking helps organise the work.

title: Indoor gardens
intro: An indoor garden develops through observation of light, growth and the conditions around each plant.

A pot and its drainage influence the conditions around roots.
New growth offers one way to observe a plant over time.
A garden notebook can record changes without rushing to conclusions.

title: Botanical observations
intro: Botanical notes describe the shapes, textures and seasonal changes visible in plants.
facts: Leaf arrangement is a useful feature to record.
Flowers and fruits may appear at different times of year.
A sketch can preserve details that are easy to overlook.
A location and date give an observation useful context.

title: Walking journals
intro: A walking journal collects the small details of a route: light, sounds, surfaces and places to pause.
facts: A short route can offer many different observations.
Time of day changes the character of a familiar place.
A sketch and a written note can complement each other.
A useful route description includes distance and terrain.

title: Coastal sketches
intro: Coastal sketching is an exercise in observing changing light, open space and the meeting of land and water.

Quick studies help record a changing atmosphere.
The viewpoint determines which details belong in the composition.

title: Bookbinding notes

A small mock-up can reveal problems in a proposed structure.

Questions can be kept alongside initial impressions.
Revisiting a note may reveal a change in interpretation.

title: Listening studies
intro: A listening notebook records impressions of rhythm, instrumentation and the way a piece develops.

Listening context can influence an impression.

title: Furniture sketches
intro: Furniture studies explore proportion, use and the relationship between an object and the space around it.
facts: A scale drawing helps compare proportions.
Materials contribute to both appearance and construction.
The intended use should inform the shape of an object.

title: Textile textures

title: Small-space studies

title: Visual storytelling
